preconditions.description: The number of sets n is between 1 and 10,000 inclusive.
The rank k is between 1 and 100 inclusive.
Both n and k are integers.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n + 1 lines: one for m and n lines for the sets.
The first line of output is the integer m.
Each of the n set lines contains exactly four space-separated integers.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= x <= m for x in set_ints) for set_ints in sets)
postconditions.description: Every integer in every set is between 1 and m inclusive.
All integers used across the n sets are distinct (no integer appears in more than one set).

postconditions.expression: all(all(gcd(a, b) == k for i, a in enumerate(s) for j, b in enumerate(s) if i < j) for s in sets)
postconditions.description: For every set, the GCD of every pair of distinct elements equals k.
The reported m is exactly the maximum integer used in the solution.
The reported m is the minimum possible value that allows constructing n valid sets of rank k.
